newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill journalist in strike-hit Karachi.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill journalist in strike-hit Karachi.

text.p: Gunmen killed a journalist and wounded an ethnic party leader in Karachi on Wednesday and a strike paralysed business activity in some areas for the second day running, police and witnesses said.

Police said unidentified assailants fired on Kamran Rizvi, a leader of the breakaway Haqiqi faction of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM), as he stepped out of his house in District Central to see off a visiting friend, Manzar Imkani, a senior sub-editor at the Urdu-language Jang newspaper.
Imkani, 49, died instantly while Rizvi, 35, was seriously wounded. Neighbours took him to hospital.
A Haqiqi spokesman accused the mainstream MQM of carrying out the attack. MQM officials denied responsibility.

Witnesses said shopping centres and state-owned bank branches in District South were closed for a a second day in a strike enforced by ethnic party militants after nine people, including five MQM activists were killed on Monday.

"We have been warned to keep shops shut on Thursday also," said a shopkeeper in Frere Road. Unidentified activists on motorcycles had said they could reopen after prayers had been said on Thursday for the five slain MQM activists, he added.
The mainstream MQM's London-based leader Altaf Hussain ordered the closure of more than 100 party offices in Karachi after Monday's deadly attack on an MQM branch.
Violence has risen in the volatile port city in recent weeks amid tension between the MQM, now part of a coalition government in Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, and Haqiqi.
More than 80 people have been killed in ethnic, political and sectarian unrest in Karachi this year, compared to 500 last year and about 2,000 in 1995.
